name: Fermilab — Batavia, Illinois
notes: Far sites (not drawn on this map; great-circle distances and bearings computed from the sourced site:fermilab-main-campus point): site:soudan-minos-far-detector (735.4 km, bearing 336.0 degrees, historical MINOS-era NuMI beam), site:ash-river-nova-far-detector (811.7 km, bearing 335.5 degrees, current NOvA-era NuMI beam), site:surf-4850-level-dune-far-detector (1287.6 km, bearing 287.7 degrees, LBNF beam). The Soudan and SURF sites have their own maps (map:soudan-underground-laboratory, map:surf); there is no map for the Ash River site. linked_map_ids on this map is empty.

The campus site (site:fermilab-main-campus, a 3 km point) is represented by the campus boundary and by the halls/points drawn at it with `site_id`; detectors placed there that could not be located are listed individually in `unlocated[]`.

detector:seaquest and site:fermilab-nm4-hall are drawn (geometry:fermilab-seaquest-point), from OpenStreetMap node 4425992583, tagged name=SeaQuest and addr:housenumber=NM4, inside the campus bounding box. A search of OpenStreetMap for the literal string 'NM4' finds nothing, which is why the experiment was first listed as unlocated; a search for the experiment's own name finds the node directly (checked 2026-09-21).

The Main Injector and Recycler are drawn (2026-10-25). The shape is computed from the TDR's straight-section lengths, dipole counts and lattice listing (derived; see geometry:fermilab-main-injector-ring for the derivation and the independent 28.789277 m check). The ring is placed with the TDR's own published site coordinates (Fermilab Site Coordinate System of Beams-doc-1148), accuracy 8 m; an earlier placement fitted to a road was displaced 38-74 m. The grassland polygon geometry:fermilab-mi-infield is context only.

summary.plain: Fermilab's main campus near Chicago, where the Booster and (until 2011) the Tevatron ring are drawn to scale from their sourced sizes, along with the Main Injector and Recycler ring, the CDF, D0, MINOS, NOvA, MiniBooNE, MicroBooNE, SBND and ICARUS detector sites and the Muon g-2 MC-1 building. The NuMI beamline and its underground halls are drawn from the NuMI design report's published coordinates; the Booster Neutrino Beam target is a derived point reconstructed from building positions and the sourced MiniBooNE distance. The 3.3 km Main Injector and Recycler ring (one shared tunnel, an oval with eight straight sections, shape from the design handbook) is drawn; PIP-II, Mu2e, the DUNE near detector and a few fixed-target detector halls could not be located precisely and are listed as unlocated. Arrows show the inferred direction of the NuMI and LBNF neutrino beams toward their far detectors in Minnesota and South Dakota, which are shown on separate maps.
summary.technical: Local to-scale map of the Fermilab Batavia campus. Rings: a derived circle for the Booster ring (474 m sourced circumference, OSM-fit centre, with the surveyed start of the 8 GeV line as an independent check) and for the Tevatron ring (6.3 km sourced circumference, centre placed from the Main Injector design handbook's survey relation and checked against the published A0 point), and the Main Injector and Recycler as derived 3319 m rings (lattice shape from the design handbook, placed with its published site coordinates; 8 m). Detectors: georeferenced OSM building footprints for the CDF Hall, D0 Assembly Building, MINOS and NOvA near-detector surface buildings, MiniBooNE Detector Building, the LArTF/MicroBooNE hall and the Muon g-2 MC-1 building, a positionally identified ICARUS-T600 hall, an OSM-tagged point for SeaQuest/NM4 and a derived point for SBND. Beams: the NuMI target, beamlines and underground halls from the NuMI design report's beam sheet (published site coordinates); a derived BNB target and beamline anchored on two independently named OSM footprints; an approximate linac axis; and inferred-direction lines for the NuMI and LBNF beams. Context features, each drawn only from a date given or bounded by a source: the campus boundary, Wilson Hall, the MI-62 service building, MC-2 and the Main Injector grassland. PIP-II, KTeV, Mu2e, MINERvA, DONUT, SENSEI, DAMIC (prototype) and the DUNE near detector are unlocated, each with a sourced reason and backlog.

unlocated.backlog: Fetch the PIP-II CDR (FERMILAB-DESIGN-2017-01) or TDR civil chapter from a mirror other than lss.fnal.gov; or the IWAA 2024 talk (Bocean) with its site-layout slide read by a person and a published azimuth/coordinate of the linac front end; or re-check OSM once PIP-II civil works are mapped (a landuse=construction polygon near the Booster would anchor the 215 m straight section).
unlocated.reason: PIP-II is under construction 'in a new tunnel with new service buildings and connected to the present Booster through a new transfer line' (src:fermilab-geo-pip-ii-radiation-2018), with a site-plan figure referenced 'with respect to Fermilab Wilson Hall'; the 2024 alignment paper adds that the tunnel 'consists of a straight section and a curved section' with 'a total beam length of approximately 550 meters' (src:fermilab-geo-pip2-iwaa2024-krawczuk) and the 2024 alignment talk gives a 210 m linac tunnel and a 300 m transfer line. No coordinates, azimuth value or dimensioned site plan could be fetched (the official CDR/TDR on lss.fnal.gov returns HTTP 403; the IWAA 2024 slides carry the site layout as an image only; an OSM extract of the campus fetched 2026-10-25 holds no PIP-II way).

unlocated.backlog: The LBNF beamline lattice or site plan in Fermilab site coordinates (FSCS/DUSAF, convertible with Beams-doc-1148 exactly as the NuMI beam sheet was): 'MI-10 Extraction Details' (LBNE-doc-10586) and the Near Site drawings (LBNE-doc-10831) are on the Fermilab DocDB (not public to scripts); an IWAA alignment paper for the LBNF beamline; or OSM mapping of the embankment and the service buildings LBNF-5, -20, -30 and -40 once they are added. The ND hall is 166 ft x 63 ft with its long axis at 90 degrees to the beam (ND CDR Table 8.1, DUNE TDR Vol. II).
unlocated.reason: No published coordinate for the LBNF target, target hall or near-detector hall was found. Published at design stage: the beam is extracted at MI-10 (LBNF CDR Vol. 3, arXiv:1601.05823); "transported 328 m (1078 ft) to the LBNF Target Complex (to the target)" (section 5.3.2) against "approximately 1,200 feet from the extraction at MI-10 to the Target Hall" (section 6.2.7) and about 1,000 ft in DOE/EA-1943; "The overall bend of the proton beam is 7.2o westward and 5.8o downward" (arXiv:1704.04471). With the Main Injector now placed from the TDR site coordinates, the MI-10 straight has heading 280.5 deg and 280.5 + 7.2 = 287.7 deg equals the great-circle bearing from MI-10 to the SURF caverns (287.76 deg), which supports the layout geometry but fixes no position: where the beam leaves the 69 m straight, which of the path lengths (305, 328 or 366 m) is as built and where the bend occurs leave the target about 50 m uncertain (chains of these figures put it at lon -88.2720 to -88.2734, lat 41.8326 to 41.8331, and the ND hall at lon -88.2786 to -88.2800, lat 41.8341 to 41.8347, from 37 m west to 78 m east of Kirk Road across the combinations, against the EA's 38-46 m from the hall's closest point). Not drawn: that is a design-stage estimate, not a position.

unlocated.backlog: Search the KTeV design report (INSPIRE literature 345348) for a hall/beamline number that could be matched to a Fermilab fixed-target-area site plan.
unlocated.reason: No OpenStreetMap footprint or other sourced coordinate for the KTeV hall was found (checked 2026-09-18; a targeted OSM name search for 'KTeV' returned no results).

unlocated.backlog: A candidate building, OSM way 720556732 'MC-2' (drawn as context only, geometry:fermilab-mc2-building), stands 84 m from the confirmed MC-1/g-2 building and is plausible given the MC-1/MC-2 naming pattern, but no fetchable text confirms MC-2 is specifically the Mu2e hall (checked 2026-09-18: a web search and two attempts to read arXiv:2208.02889 'Muon Campus at Fermilab', HTML and PDF). Re-checked 2026-10-25: the Mu2e TDR (arXiv:1501.05241, Fig. 6.120 and sections 1-2) and the Muon Campus overview (arXiv:2208.02889) contain no site coordinate and do not name the Mu2e building MC-2; further web searches for 'MC-2' with Mu2e found no source. The former Antiproton Source buildings AP-0/AP-10/AP-30/AP-50 (OSM, src:fermilab-geo-osm-muon-campus) cluster near 41.8346,-88.2656 and are candidate anchors for the adjacent Delivery Ring (ex-Debuncher), but no source consulted (checked 2026-09-18) states the ring's shape or circumference, and three building centroids are not enough to justify drawing a ring without a sourced vertex/side correspondence, so it is not drawn. Confirming either would let Mu2e become a drawn `hall`. Next: Fermilab's facilities directory or a Muon Campus site plan that names the Mu2e building, or the Mu2e Offline geometry text files (world coordinates of the hall).
unlocated.reason: No OpenStreetMap footprint is confirmed for the Mu2e building specifically (a targeted OSM name search for 'Mu2e' found none); the Mu2e TDR (src:muons-arxiv-1501-05241) describes the production/transport/detector solenoid dimensions and states the Mu2e building shares a berm/enclosure with the Delivery Ring extraction beamline (the M4 beamline), but gives no single coordinate or scalar distance from a fixed point.

unlocated.backlog: The MINERvA detector paper (NIM A743, arXiv:1305.5199) section on the detector location for the offset of its upstream face from the hall's upstream end; the hall is 150 ft long and the TDR puts the MINOS detector face 85.5 ft inside it, so MINERvA sits in the first ~85 ft.
unlocated.reason: MINERvA stood in the MINOS near-detector hall, which is now drawn (geometry:fermilab-minos-near-hall, from the NuMI TDR beam sheet); the NuMI paper confirms the cavern "subsequently housed additional experiments such as MINERvA or ArgoNeuT". The position of the MINERvA detector inside the hall is not published in a source fetched.

unlocated.backlog: Find a DONUT (E872) technical note with a beamline/hall number that could be matched to a Fermilab fixed-target-area site plan.
unlocated.reason: No dedicated OpenStreetMap footprint or other sourced coordinate for the DONUT hall was found (checked 2026-09-18); the existing placement record for this 1997 fixed-target experiment uses the Fermilab main-campus point because the DONUT paper gives only the beamline layout, not a coordinate.

unlocated.backlog: The SENSEI/MINOS-hall installation paper or the Fermilab experiment page for the position of the SENSEI cryostat in the hall.
unlocated.reason: SENSEI's prototype was placed in the MINOS cavern (existing placement record, src:sensei-shallow-underground-2019-arxiv), which is now drawn (geometry:fermilab-minos-near-hall); its position inside the hall is not published.

unlocated.backlog: Find a DAMIC prototype technical note giving its Fermilab hall location.
unlocated.reason: The original DAMIC prototype's Fermilab placement (2008-2012) has no dedicated hall coordinate in the sources consulted (checked 2026-09-18); the existing placement record notes only that a precise coordinate was not found.

unlocated.backlog: Same backlog as beamline:lbnf: once the target (or the hall) has a published site coordinate, the hall follows from 574 m along the bearing to SURF (287.7 deg) and its 166 ft x 63 ft size.
unlocated.reason: The DUNE near detector hall is sourced at 574 m ("about 570 m") from the LBNF target, 60 m deep, "on the western-most boundary of Fermi National Laboratory" and "125-150 feet east of Kirk Road at its closest point" (DOE/EA-1943), 166 ft x 63 ft with its long axis at 90 degrees to the beam (ND CDR Table 8.1; DUNE TDR Vol. II); but the LBNF target it is measured from has no published coordinate (see beamline:lbnf), and chaining the figures leaves the hall about 50 m uncertain, too coarse for a 50 m hall.
detector:ktev, the only detector placed at this site, is unlocated (see above); the site itself is not drawn either.
